This phone may stop the app once you switch away
Let it keep running in the background
Not on WiFi or a hotspot
This phone has not measured its own lead, so it will sound before the others
Tens of ms out, and you can hear it
%1$s may be held back by battery saving
Background running allowed on this phone
Phones already connected will drop and have to scan again.
On the other phone, open the app, pick Be a sink, and scan this code
This phone has no address another phone could reach. Join a WiFi network, or turn on a hotspot.
No other device has connected yet. Pick Be a sink on another device and it connects by itself.
Select a device to calibrate it on its own.
Fine calibration makes the error smaller but takes longer. Each phone only needs it once.
Nothing heard for a while; the screen is probably off
That phone was there a moment ago and cannot be reached now.
No other device is connected yet. On the other devices, choose Be a sink, and make sure they are on the same network. If they do not connect by themselves, scan the host\'s QR code from each sink.
This phone\'s output delay has not been measured. Playing now will be out of sync and sound worse. Go on anyway?
Not calibrated, or calibration failed: %1$s. Playback may be out of sync and sound worse. Go on anyway?
Only needed when the room plays what this phone is playing.
Measures where each phone is and syncs their clocks.
Measured. If a phone has moved, you can calibrate again.
Battery saving stopped the app on that phone
Allow background running on that phone first

Allowed, and stopped anyway. On that phone, open the system settings, find app launch management, set this app to manual, and turn all three switches on. Nothing can read those three switches or turn them on for you.
A network may only have one host. To move it, make the current host a sink first.
The source: other devices play in sync with this one
Plays the host\'s sound in sync
Capture what this phone is playing
Capturing what this phone is playing

Turn this phone\'s media volume down to 0, then play from your own music app. What is captured comes out about 1 s later, together with the other phones; leave media up and you will hear it twice. This phone\'s own copy goes out on the alarm channel, and the slider below sets how loud.
Without the microphone permission this phone cannot capture its own audio. Turn it on for this app in the system settings.
The capture was not granted, or the grant has been taken back.
Measure once, and you never need to do this again
Leave the phone on a table untouched and keep the room quiet, about a minute and a half.
Keep as quiet as you can
About a minute and a half. Leave the phone alone.
Measuring again will not be more accurate, unless something interfered last time.
Repeatability run finished (diagnostic, nothing stored): median %1$.3f ms, spread %2$.3f ms, readable pairs %3$d.
Verified: %1$.3f ms left after the correction. The closer to zero, the better the stored number.
This measurement failed. Put the phone on a table, do not touch it while it runs, keep the room quiet, and try turning the volume up
Without the microphone permission there is nothing to measure with: the phone has to hear itself. Turn it on for this app in the system settings.
Drag the slider below to set the volume of both outputs
%1$s is too low. Take it past %2$d%%.
Stopping now silences this phone at once, and this round\'s data is void.
This round was cancelled and the data is void.
This phone has not scanned the other one\'s code. Go back and scan it once.
Go back and say whether this phone is the host or a sink.
Put the two phones within arm\'s reach of each other
, with nothing in between. About a minute, and keep it quiet
Check what has already been measured
Drag the icons to roughly where they stand, then tap Fit to measurement
The same drawing as the playback screen: dragging is you saying where this phone stands, and Fit to measurement moves the drawing onto the shape that was measured. The two always agree.
Connecting: waiting for the other phone.
Connecting: syncing clocks with the other phone, about 16 s. Nothing sounds in this step.
Syncing clocks with the other phone. Nothing sounds in this step.
Measuring: leave both phones alone and keep it quiet.
Working it out; a few seconds.
Calibration syncs the devices\' clocks and measures the distances, so volume and timing can be set properly.
Drag this slider to set every phone\'s volume, so they can all hear each other.
%1$s too quiet. Keep the volume above %2$d%%
Hold the host; put the other phones where you want to hear them
Sit where you listen and hold this phone above your head, with nothing between it and the other phones
Press start; it sounds a few seconds later, and you can put it down when it ends
You can skip it, but then where your ears are is not measured.
Put this phone back where it belongs too
Touch none of the phones, and keep people and things out from between them
Press start; they sound one after another a few seconds later
Checks the sound is good enough
This device sounded too quiet. Turn it up, or check nothing is in the way
If the phones moved, the listening position from step 1 is out of date as well. Redo both.
Keep as quiet as you can
The host starts this round and this device measures in sync. Nothing to press here.
Told %1$d, waiting for them to dial in, up to %2$d s. They start on their own; nothing to press.
%1$d dialled in of %2$d told. When the two match, just wait: they are busy.

**Nobody was told, so no phone will start.** The others have to have this app open and be sitting on its front screen to get the command. On the launcher, in another app, or still on the last round\'s result page, and it never arrives. Take them all back to the front screen, where it says how many are standing by, and press again.
%1$d in the room; %2$d of %3$d pairs measured.
No microphone permission. Grant it first, then measure.
This device\'s network round trip to this host is too slow; the number would be unusable.
This device\'s clock has not converged, which is usually the network as well.
This device is in the middle of another measurement. Press again when it finishes.
This device is standing by, but its screen is off. Playback and volume do not need the screen; measuring does. Wake that phone and press again.
The microphone is muted or its input volume is 0. Change it in the system settings.
Delivered. %1$d in the room, %2$d pairs measured for this phone.

Delivered. %1$d in the room, %2$d pairs measured for this phone. This phone has never been properly synced with the host, so the %3$.3f ms this round worked out has been kept to be going on with. It is an estimate, out by 1–2 ms. Press Start sync when there is time and a real measurement will replace it.
This round was cancelled and the data is void.
Stopping now silences both phones at once, and this round\'s data is void.
Nothing has sounded yet. Cancel now and every phone goes back to its front screen.
Cancelling now silences every phone in the room at once, and this round\'s data is void.
This round was cancelled, every phone in the room heard it, and the data is void.
Offset %1$.3f ms, about %2$.2f m apart. Calibrated
Measured: about %1$.2f m apart. You can put the phones down.
Done: this pair is %1$.3f ms apart, and it has been stored (observation %2$d).

This network is too slow to align on: a round trip between the two phones takes %1$.0f ms, and past %2$.0f nothing lines up. If this phone is running the hotspot, let the other one run it and join that instead; if both are on a router, have one run a hotspot and the other join it.
Clear this pair\'s calibration and start over
What is stored is %1$.3f ms, the average of %2$d observations. Clearing it is final; the next round starts from nothing, about a minute.
Cleared. The next round will take its result whole, the way the first one did.
Verified: %1$.3f ms left after the correction. The closer to zero, the better the stored number.
The result came from another phone (%1$s), not the one this round was arranged with, so it was not folded in. Let that phone finish, or start this round again.
Experimental round (the link gate was bypassed): the offset measured was %1$.3f ms. The data is stored, but it has **not** been folded into this pair\'s correction.
This round does not count and was not stored: %1$s
This round came out %1$.1f ms away from what is stored, too far, so it was thrown away as a bad round and the stored number is untouched. Measure again.
Without the microphone permission there is nothing to measure with: the phone has to hear the other one. Turn it on for this app in the system settings.
Captured playback goes out on the alarm channel, whose volume is separate from media. The volume keys set it while this page is open, or find the alarm volume under Settings → Sound.
This phone is capturing another app. To avoid hearing it twice, it is playing on the alarm channel for now, and the alarm volume is put back afterwards.
Turn media volume down to 1 or lower, or you will hear everything twice
How it works: start playing in the other app first, then come back here and tap “Play”. Keep media volume at 0 throughout, or you will hear everything twice
%1$s took the command but has never reported its own volume back, so the number beside it is old.
Sound has been paused for %1$d s. If you did not pause it yourself, try setting this handset\'s media volume to 1.
Press back when it has scanned
Point this phone at the code on the host\'s screen; it scans by itself.
That is a code, but not this app\'s
No camera permission. Turn it on in the settings and come back to this page.
For %1$d of them the number came out of a room round rather than a proper sync. That is about 1–2 ms out, too little to hear, but worth measuring properly when there is time.
Not synced with this phone: %1$d. Without a sync the offset is taken as zero, so they will be tens of ms out, which you can hear. Go to those phones and run Sync with the paired phone once on each.
Connected. This device plays by itself once the host starts playing.
This phone is not on WiFi. Join the same network as the host, or the hotspot the host is running.
This phone and the host are on different networks: the host is on %1$s, this phone on %2$s. Some routers split 2.4G and 5G into two networks, and a guest network is another one again.

Same network as the host, but no connection. Either the host does not have this app open, or the network does not let devices talk to each other, which campus, office and public networks often do not. The surest way round it is a hotspot on the host with this phone joining it.
No host yet; looking for one on this network. If nothing turns up, scan the code on the host\'s screen. Some networks do not let devices find each other on their own.
This phone has no address the other one could reach
Playing together, but the sync has degraded
The file is gone. Choose another song.
Nothing in this folder can be played
There is no audio track in this file
This song is shorter than a single block
The decoder stalled. Try another song.
The decoder did not say what format this song is in
This song\'s decoded format cannot be played: 16-bit PCM is needed, at 8 to 96 kHz
This song has more than two channels, 5.1 surround for instance, and this version plays stereo only
Spread the phones evenly around you; it sounds better that way
If a phone has moved a long way, drag its icon to where it is now, which changes what you hear. For a proper job, calibrate again.
Every phone plays the same thing, together
Phones on the left play the left channel and phones on the right the right, split by the layout above.
The source circles around you; better with three phones or more
Drag the white dot on the layout above to move the source
Tap the icons on the layout above to change which phone plays what.
Live readings: the phone with the bigger number is where the sound should be
The dot joined to you on the layout is the source. Drag it to move the sound.
The source sits on the ring of phones; the room is as it was.
The source is inside the ring of phones: direction is %1$d%% weaker.

But the room has no reverb at all right now, so pulling it back only makes it quieter. Loudness alone cannot say how far away something is — a whisper at your ear and a shout across the street can be equally loud. Turn up Room reverb below: the reverb does not recede with the source, so one drops and the other does not, and the ear reads that as distance.
Envelopment: how much a phone keeps once the sound turns away
Hard left: a phone the sound has turned away from goes silent, which sounds like one phone turning.
Further right is more enveloping and less directional.
This only works well on some music; it depends on the recording
Crossover: below %1$d Hz counts as bass
No other phone has connected. One phone can be placed, but there is no direction to hear.
The icons have been set from the measurement. Drag any phone to do it again.
Held back so they arrive together (ms)
Where you sit has not been measured, so the drawing puts you in the middle. Measure it and the volumes and the timing are worked out from where you actually are.
Measure where I sit (hold it overhead)
The measurement says %1$s is further away than %2$s, and your drawing says the opposite. Are those two icons the wrong way round?
Will not start: the sync and the playback use the same port, and the sync is probably still open. Press stop on the sync page, wait a few seconds, and try again.
Turn a few devices into one set of speakers
This app on each of them
Send it to the phone beside you
You can come back here to change roles.
The other phone picks Be a sink
The other phone picks Be the host
Have the other phone scan this code
This code is for phones on this phone\'s hotspot
This code is for phones on the same WiFi
Shows diagnostic readings such as the clock offset. Not needed day to day.
Recording is used only while calibrating or playing this phone\'s own sound, and at no other time
Shows what is going on, and keeps the system from stopping it
Only to scan the other phone\'s pairing code; no photos are kept
Without it the connection may drop when you switch away
Anything refused on the first launch can be granted here. Anything refused twice is handed to the system settings.
